title: Cobalt Springs Onboarding Kickoff & Runway Sync
meeting_header:
Date: 2026-03-29
Start: 08:43 PT
Duration: ~52m
Location: Zoom
Recordings: zoom-link-placeholder
Attendees: Avery Chen, Jordan Morales, Priya Nair (Redwood) — Lena Ortiz, Rajiv Singh, Samira Cole, Ben Torres (Cobalt Springs)
summary: Kickoff to align on onboarding runway for Cobalt Springs Health pilot. Covered high-level timeline, success criteria, network/VPC requirements, data residency and security checklist (SOC2 scope, KMS), and an initial plan for a 4-week pilot (non-prod) followed by a production readiness checklist. SE and Infra discussed perf expectations, batching and cache strategies; customer requested a simple benchmark plan and an SSO integration timeline. Next actions: share onboarding runbook, security pack, and schedule a 1-day performance benchmark with sample prompts.
transcript:
[00:00] Avery Chen: hey everyone good morning thanks for joining really appreciate you making time. can everyone hear me?
[00:04] Lena Ortiz: yes loud and clear, thanks avery.
[00:07] Rajiv Singh: yep, good morning all.
[00:09] Priya Nair: morning! we'll keep this tight, agenda in chat.
[00:15] Avery Chen: cool so i'll run through the kickoff goals — align scope for the pilot, get any blockers on security/networking up front, and schedule bench + handoffs. jordan do you wanna take perf and infra high level?
[00:27] Jordan Morales: sure. hi folks im jordan, i'm the solutions engineer on the account. quick context — redwood supports hosted, dedicated, and private deployments; for pilots we typically recommend either hosted with VPC peering or private light (managed control plane with customer VPC) depending on data sensitivity.
[00:45] Ben Torres: quick q — for pilot do we need to provide data or can we use synthetic?
[00:50] Jordan Morales: synthetic is fine for initial perf tests, but for quality/regression you'll want a small redacted sample set. performance won't change much with real vs synthetic unless you have long contexts or multimodal attachments.
[01:05] Rajiv Singh: our primary constraint is we need egress locked down; we cannot allow traffic out of our VPC except to specific endpoints. also prefer keys stored in our KMS.
[01:16] Samira Cole: and we need SOC 2 artifacts and an audit log retention policy — what do you provide there?
[01:24] Avery Chen: we have a security pack — SOC 2 type II summary, ISO docs, and an audit log export; we'll share the pack after this meeting. for KMS we support customer-managed keys in the private deployment and in dedicated with HSM integrations. the hosted default uses redwood-managed keys but we can do customer KMS for enterprise.
[01:41] Lena Ortiz: timeline — we're aiming to validate the inference path and latency with ~1000 qps sim over a 2 hour window by mid april. is that realistic?
[01:50] Jordan Morales: for 1000 qps we should talk about dedicated capacity; hosted can burst but not guarantee. there are knobs — batching, sequence length tuning, KV cache — that can help. quick question: what model family and avg token length are you targeting?
[02:06] Ben Torres: targeted model is an open Llama-variant we've been trialing, average seq length 64 tokens, but some long ones up to 512.
[02:14] Jordan Morales: OK long tails to 512 will increase mem footprint and affect latency; we typically recommend configuring an autoscale headroom for bursts. we can run a benchmark on a dedicated pool candidate and show p99 numbers.
[02:28] Priya Nair: i'll add note — success metrics from cotside? lena?
[02:32] Lena Ortiz: success is: p95 < 220ms for median batch workload, p99 < 800ms under expected load for short requests; accuracy/regression measured via our prompt set with 95% pass rate. plus no data exfil / logs left outside our control.
[02:48] Samira Cole: yep plus SSO into console via SAML is required before production.
[02:52] Avery Chen: all doable — SAML SSO is standard enterprise flow. we usually schedule SSO in week 3 of onboarding. for the no-exfil constraint private deployment or dedicated with customer KMS would be recommended.
[03:05] Rajiv Singh: so next steps — network ACLs, IP allowlist, and a service account we can use for peering?
[03:12] Jordan Morales: correct, we'll provide a runbook with the exact CIDR/IPs and connectivity steps. for private deployment we'll need an initial infra template and onboarding checklist.
[03:22] Ben Torres: cost perspective — is dedicated fixed monthly or billed per token? we want numbers to compare.
[03:28] Avery Chen: dedicated is reserved capacity with commit tiers; hosted is per-use. we'll send an estimated cost model for your workload after we get the benchmark numbers. for pilot we can propose a small dedicated pool if you want guaranteed throughput.
[03:42] Lena Ortiz: timeline again — mid april test. does that leave enough time for SSO and security review?
[03:49] Samira Cole: security team will need the SOC docs and a short questionnaire — can you share the questionnaire now?
[03:55] Priya Nair: yes we'll send the security questionnaire along with SOC2 + network runbook within 24 hours.
[04:02] [04:02] Speaker label glitch: Speaker 1: i think we should also plan a 1 day onsite or deep benchmark day to run real payloads and watch live metrics
[04:12] Jordan Morales: agreed — let's plan a 'benchmark day' where we run your sample prompts, measure p50/p95/p99 and error behavior. i propose week of april 13th.
[04:21] Rajiv Singh: april 13th could work. we'll need to blackhole outgoing S3 so nothing leaves, i'm serious about that.
[04:27] Avery Chen: understood. for pilot we can do everything in non-prod VPC and avoid any data shipping. we also support prefix/KV cache controls so state doesn't leak.
[04:38] Ben Torres: can you explain the rollout plan? what does go-live look like after pilot?
[04:42] Priya Nair: typically pilot → staging ramp → production. pilot is 3-4 weeks to validate perf and quality, staging is a gradual cutover with canaries and routing policies, then production full rollout. we can break down dates after bench day.
[04:58] Lena Ortiz: stakeholders — i'll own product/quality, rajiv infra, samira security. you'll want a single slack channel?
[05:05] Avery Chen: yes please — we'll ask you to invite ae, se, csm and the engineers. also will send calendar invites for the benchmark day and a technical deep dive after runbook review.
[05:16] Jordan Morales: quick technical note — if you're planning long-context requests to 512 we should discuss KV cache and offloading. also tokenizer differences across Llama forks sometimes cause subtle perf/quality diffs; we'll validate with your model binary on the bench day.
[05:33] Rajiv Singh: model binary — can redwood host our private model artifact or do we need to provide a fork?
[05:38] Jordan Morales: we can host a model in dedicated or private as a customer model; for hosted we'd need to vet licensing. for private deployment you keep total control. we'll share the onboarding step to upload model artifacts securely (s3 presigned or direct transfer into your VPC).
[05:54] Samira Cole: about logs — retention duration, who can access them?
[05:58] Avery Chen: logs are tenant-scoped; you can configure retention and role-based access. audit log exports can be pushed to your S3 and encrypted with your KMS. we'll include sample policies in the runbook.
[06:12] Ben Torres: competitor question — we previously evaluated AtlasAI and CloudNode; any differences we should call out?
[06:20] Avery Chen: sure — AtlasAI has strong model access but less production telemetry; CloudNode offers on-prem but lacks continuous batching/token-level cost breakdowns. redwood focuses on predictable inference economics and developer experience for production.
[06:36] [06:36] Jordan Morales: (murmured) also note that kernel & compilation tuning is a differentiator for us — helps with those long-tail sequences.
[06:45] Lena Ortiz: ok good. can you share an early diagram of the private deployment topology?
[06:49] Priya Nair: yes — we'll attach a network diagram in the runbook.
[06:53] [07:00] Jordan Morales: technical deep dive item — can we get your test dataset and example prompt set ahead of the bench day? small redacted set is fine. that lets us pre-tune batching and warm caches.
[07:12] Lena Ortiz: yes we'll send 200 sample prompts, redacted.
[07:16] Rajiv Singh: we also need to see how autoscaling behaves — can you simulate sustained load?
[07:21] Jordan Morales: yes we can run a sustained throughput simulation; for dedicated we can demonstrate scaling policies.
[07:29] [07:29] Speaker 2 (auto-label): um one point — dcs latency from eu-west region showed jitter last week on your public benchmarks, is that expected?
[07:36] Avery Chen: thanks for calling that out — network jitter can come from path and peering; we'll plan region-specific bench runs and recommend colocated capacity if you have EU users.
[07:48] Ben Torres: data residency — we need EU data to remain in eu-west. is that supported?
[07:53] Avery Chen: yes, we support region pinning and you can host private controllers in-region for full residency. we'll include that in options.
[07:59] Samira Cole: can we get an export of the compliance questionnaires answered by redwood?
[08:03] Priya Nair: yes we'll attach the completed questionnaire and a SOC2 snapshot in the follow-up.
[08:09] [08:30] Jordan Morales: flipping to pilot acceptance — what's the minimal pass for you?
[08:34] Lena Ortiz: acceptance = latency targets met + accuracy on our eval harness + SSO and audit logs validated.
[08:41] Rajiv Singh: and network isolation validated (no egress) in non-prod.
[08:46] Avery Chen: good. i'll share an acceptance checklist.
[08:49] Ben Torres: any blockers on our side?
[08:51] Lena Ortiz: we'll need legal to sign the DPA — can you send draft?
[08:55] Priya Nair: yes we'll send draft DPA and contract points to your legal contact, include our standard pilot terms.
[09:01] [09:12] Jordan Morales: technical note on batching — if you have lots of short requests we can combine into micro-batches to reduce cost without impacting p95 too much. we'll show config tradeoffs on bench day.
[09:24] Rajiv Singh: what about model quantization? does that reduce quality?
[09:28] Jordan Morales: quantization can affect some models; our Optimize team will run a QC matrix and provide recommended quant levels per model to balance cost and quality.
[09:36] Avery Chen: we're at about 10 minutes of notes — should we move to next steps and owners?
[09:42] Priya Nair: yes.
[09:44] Avery Chen: ok action items — i'll recap then priya will record.
[09:48] Priya Nair: noted.
[09:49] Avery Chen: action 1: redwood to send runbook, security pack (SOC2 + questionnaire), network CIDRs, and DPA draft within 24 hours. owner: Avery / Priya.
[09:59] Priya Nair: action 2: cobalt springs to share 200-sample prompt set and target workload profile. owner: Lena / Rajiv. due: 2026-04-06.
[10:11] Avery Chen: action 3: schedule benchmark day week of 2026-04-13 — target apr 15 tentative. owner: Jordan + Rajiv.
[10:22] Priya Nair: action 4: security to review and confirm KMS approach — owner: Samira. due: 2026-04-09.
[10:34] Ben Torres: action 5: legal to review DPA — owner: Ben (legal). due: 2026-04-08.
[10:43] [10:50] Jordan Morales: i'll prep a perf plan showing expected p50/p95/p99 ranges for short and long sequences and share before the bench day.
[10:58] Lena Ortiz: great, thanks jordan.
[11:02] Samira Cole: one more question — do you support fine-grained RBAC for console access?
[11:07] Avery Chen: yes RBAC with roles mapped via SAML, we can lock down model uploads and logs to specific roles. we'll include sample role mappings.
[11:18] Ben Torres: ok thats helpful.
[11:20] Priya Nair: i'll send a follow-up email with all attachments and calendar invites; please reply to confirm the bench date.
[11:28] Lena Ortiz: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[11:31] Avery Chen: thanks all, we'll follow up within 24 hours.
[11:34] [11:34] Meeting closed.
